Let <MATH_0001> be a field.
Unramified quasi-compact morphisms <MATH_0002> are affine.
This is true because <MATH_0003> has dimension <MATH_0004> and is Noetherian,
hence is a finite discrete set, and each point gives an affine open,
so <MATH_0005> is a finite disjoint union of affines hence affine.
Noether normalization forces <MATH_0006> to be the spectrum of a finite
<MATH_0007>-algebra <MATH_0008>.
This algebra is a product of finite separable field extensions of <MATH_0009>.
Thus, an unramified quasi-compact morphism to <MATH_0010>
corresponds to a finite number of finite separable field extensions of <MATH_0011>.
In particular, an unramified morphism with a connected source and a one point
target is forced to be a finite separable field extension.
As we will see later, <MATH_0012> is <ACCENT_0001>tale if and
only if it is unramified. Thus, in this case at least, we obtain a very easy
description of the <ACCENT_0002>tale topology of a scheme. Of course, the cohomology of
this topology is another story.
